newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Feb industrial production.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Feb industrial production.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' and analysts' initial reactions to Japan's February industrial production, which showed a month-on-month fall of 3.4 percent, in line with economists' average forecast of a 3.3 percent fall.
MIKIHIRO MATSUOKA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DAIWA INSTITUTE OF RESEARCH:

Asked whether the February data was an adjustment from January figures, Matsuoka said: "That's correct. In past years, we had a very strong number in the first month of every quarter, followed by declines in the second and third months of the quarter."
Producers are usually too optimistic about their production plans at the beginning of the year, but then revise down their plans throughout the year, Matsuoka said.
TAKASHI KIUCHI, CHIEF ECONOMIST, LONG-TERM CREDIT BANK OF JAPAN:

Asked whether the February output figure was affected by a break in car production due to a fire at car parts maker Aisin Seiki, Kiuchi said: "The disruption in car output was contained fairly well so as not to show a catastrophic fall in industrial production."
Kiuchi said February's negative production figure, along with a forecast fall in manufacturers' output in March, do not necessarily form a trend, adding the focus was on the forecast for April.
"A 1.0 plus (figure) is confirmation that the corporate sector is still positive about sales after April and is willing to increase production."
Manufacturers' output for April is expected to show a rise of 1.0 percent.
SUSUMU KATO, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT BZW SECURITIES JAPAN LTD:

"The February data fell on an adjustment from January's 5.6 percent increase. The drop was also partly due to fewer business days than other months and also because the previous year was a leap year."
He said the drop in the production data was also due to the fire at Aisin Seiki, which MITI had said would push down production by one percentage point.
"Aside from these (factors), I would say that production is relatively firm.
"The economic conditions are already firm now. People say the economy will slowdown in April to June period, but from the perspective of production, I don't think it will fall drastically.
"Exports have recovered and orders are also good. Production in April and May is expected to be pretty solid."
